summary: Per-template fact caching (use_fact_cache=True) stores each host's ansible_facts in the controller so --limit jobs can still read facts for the whole inventory; Per-Host Ansible Fact Cache Timeout is in Settings > Automation Execution > Job, changes are logged to the system_tracking logger, and hostnames containing / are not cached.
questions: How does fact caching work in automation controller?
How do I set the fact cache timeout in AAP?
Why are facts not cached for one host?
Can I use cached facts with --limit?

answer_card.title: Fact caching in controller
answer_card.answer_md:
- Enable **Enable fact storage** on the job template (`use_fact_cache=True`). It is off by default.
- After the job, each host's `ansible_facts` are stored in controller; later jobs (even with `--limit`) can read facts for all hosts in the inventory.
- Set a per-host expiry in **Settings > Automation Execution > Job > Per-Host Ansible Fact Cache Timeout** (seconds).
- New or changed facts are logged to the `system_tracking` logger with `host_name`, `inventory_id`, `ansible_facts`.
- Hosts with `/` in the name are not cached.
